title: Guided Cultural Experience — Tsuut’ina Museum
body:
Tsuut’ina Nation · Guided · By request
Duration: Custom
Meets: Museum
Cost: Custom
Begin with an immersive introduction to Tsuut’ina culture through storytelling, history, language and traditions. Knowledgeable cultural guides help visitors understand the Nation from its own cultural perspective and connect historical knowledge with living traditions.
Highlights
 Guided by knowledgeable cultural interpreters
 Introduction to Tsuut’ina history and storytelling
 Learn about language and traditions
 Cultural Museum and Gift Shop experience

title: Buffalo Paddock Tour
body:
Tsuut’ina Nation · Outdoor · Guided
Duration: Custom
Meets: By arrangement
Cost: Custom
Visit the Tsuut’ina buffalo herd and discover the deep cultural and historical relationship between the buffalo, the land and the Nation. The outdoor experience combines observation with guided interpretation and cultural learning.
Highlights
 Visit the Tsuut’ina buffalo herd
 Learn about the cultural importance of buffalo
 Connection between land and tradition
 Scenic outdoor setting
 Guided interpretation

title: Tsuut’ina Museum & Gift Shop
body:
Tsuut’ina Nation · Museum · Cultural stop
Visit: 1–2 hrs
Type: Museum
Setting: Indoor
A meaningful stop for visitors who want to explore Tsuut’ina history and contemporary culture in greater depth. Exhibits, stories and cultural interpretation introduce the Nation’s heritage, while the gift shop showcases Indigenous-made clothing, jewellery, moccasins and other works.
Highlights
 Tsuut’ina history and cultural exhibits
 Indigenous storytelling and interpretation
 Nation-owned gift shop
 Work from Indigenous artisans
 Accessible visitor experience

title: Weaselhead Flats Natural Environment Park
body:
Nearby · Nature park · Walking
Visit: 1–3 hrs
Type: Outdoors
Cost: Free
A large natural area near the western side of Calgary where the Elbow River enters the Glenmore Reservoir. Forest, wetlands, pathways and wildlife make it a good option for a quiet walk after exploring the resort and surrounding Tsuut’ina area.
Highlights
 Walking and nature trails
 Wetland and forest environments
 Birdwatching opportunities
 Connections to Glenmore Reservoir pathways

title: Heritage Park Historical Village
body:
Nearby · Living history · Family visit
Visit: 2–4 hrs
Type: Historical Park
Setting: Indoor & Outdoor
Explore Western Canadian history through historic buildings, recreated streets, exhibitions and interactive experiences. The large open-air museum presents several periods of regional history and works well as a longer half-day excursion.
Highlights
 Historic buildings and recreated streets
 Living-history experiences
 Transportation and railway heritage
 Indoor and outdoor exhibitions
 Suitable for a longer visit

title: The Military Museums
body:
Nearby · Calgary · History
Visit: 1–3 hrs
Type: Museum
Setting: Indoor
Explore Canadian military history through galleries dedicated to the Army, Royal Canadian Navy and Royal Canadian Air Force. Collections include uniforms, vehicles, aircraft, documents and historical objects connected with Canada and Alberta.
Highlights
 Army, Navy and Air Force galleries
 Historic military vehicles and equipment
 Alberta military history
 Permanent exhibitions

title: Seven Chiefs Sportsplex & Jim Starlight Centre
body:
Tsuut’ina Nation · Recreation · Community
Visit: Varies
Type: Sportsplex
Setting: Indoor
A major Tsuut’ina Nation recreation and community facility that hosts sports, gatherings and community activities. It represents another side of contemporary Nation life beyond the resort and cultural-tour experience.
Highlights
 Tsuut’ina Nation community facility
 Sports and recreation spaces
 Community gatherings and events
 Contemporary Nation setting

title: Taza Park
body:
Nearby · Tsuut’ina Nation · Modern destination
Visit: Flexible
Type: Mixed-use district
Setting: Urban
Explore one of the major contemporary development areas on Tsuut’ina Nation. Taza represents the modern economic and commercial side of the Nation and offers another perspective on how Tsuut’ina continues to grow alongside Calgary.
Highlights
 Located on Tsuut’ina Nation
 Modern commercial development
 Shopping and services nearby
 Easy addition to a Grey Eagle visit

title: Fish Creek Provincial Park
body:
Calgary · Provincial park · Outdoor
Visit: 1–4 hrs
Type: Nature
Cost: Free
One of Calgary’s largest natural recreation areas, offering extensive pathways, river landscapes, forests and open spaces. It is a good choice for visitors who want to add hiking, cycling or a relaxed outdoor stop to their stay.
Highlights
 Extensive walking and cycling trails
 River and natural landscapes
 Picnic and recreation areas
 Wildlife observation
 Multiple park access points
